initialize.instructions:
Palmier Pro exposes the open project through filmmaker-oriented tools. Use current tool schemas and
returned state for exact capabilities. These instructions describe shared semantics; they do not grant
authorization for unrelated edits or spending.

For questions about using Palmier Pro, consult https://www.palmier.io/llms.txt and its relevant linked
guide when web access is available. If the docs do not answer the question, say so rather than guess.

## Project and time model

- Timeline positions and durations use project frames; source positions use seconds. Ranges are
  half-open. Prefer tool-provided source spans and timeline mappings. If a calculation is required,
  distinguish source offset, timeline placement, trim, and speed, and use the current tool's documented
  conversion. Do not invent frame values from rounded display durations.
- Tracks are typed video/audio; index 0 composites on top. Use stable track IDs for management because
  indexes change. Images and text use video tracks. A nested sequence is mediaType `sequence`.
- Pass IDs back exactly as returned. A clip ID, media ID, timeline ID, marker ID, caption group ID, and
  linked-audio ID identify different entities. Video placement includes linked audio by default; use
  `includeAudio=false` when the source sound is unwanted.
- Tools target the session's active timeline. Use `get_media` for timelines, `create_timeline(from=...)`
  for an alternate version, and `set_active_timeline` to switch. Re-read after switching. Honor project
  visibility/session-binding refusals; do not silently retarget another project.

## Read and verify

- Establish current structure with `get_timeline` and relevant assets with `get_media`. During an
  uninterrupted edit sequence, patch your working view from mutation deltas. Re-read at verification
  boundaries and after outside changes, a stale-state error, or a wait that could change the target.
- Use `search_media` to locate material. Use spoken scope for dialogue searches. Inspect actual assets
  before describing or selecting them; use overview and transcript segments to narrow long material,
  then inspect relevant ranges.
- `get_transcript` reflects the current timeline; `inspect_media` describes a source. Word indices must
  be refreshed after cutting. Segment summaries do not expose every seam fragment or retake.
  Read word-level dialogue as prose before selecting removals and re-read it after cutting. Check
  suspicious seam fragments against word timings rather than trusting the summary.
- Transcription language follows the spoken material. Cloud transcription auto-detects; local
  transcription uses a BCP-47 language. Pass an explicitly known language for non-English local work;
  if it is unknown and local output is wrong, clarify it before a corrected retry.
- `inspect_timeline` inspects composited frames; `inspect_media` inspects source frames. Their
  coordinate grids have a top-left origin. Sample close to relevant boundaries. Frame samples and
  transcripts do not constitute audiovisual playback verification.
- `inspect_color` supplies scopes and frames for color decisions. Statistics are measurements, not
  instructions to neutralize intentional lighting or make unlike scenes numerically identical.

## Shared edit operations

- Use existing domain operations, including linked-clip handling and undo. Resolve targets before
  mutating; do not emulate timeline changes by writing project files. Several tool calls do not
  automatically form one atomic undo action.
- Use `remove_words` for transcript-aligned removals, `remove_silence` for intended pause cleanup, and
  `ripple_delete_ranges` for other ranges. Choose the editorial removals before choosing the tool.
  `split_clips` adds boundaries without closing gaps. Refresh transcript indices after removals.
  When using pause cleanup, choose `minimumPauseSeconds` and `speechPaddingSeconds` for the intended
  delivery; preserve breathing and word boundaries instead of minimizing every gap.
- Use `apply_layout` for composition, split screen, PIP, and grid, including its supported motion. Fix
  occlusion by track ordering. Use source crop for source cropping and keyframes for supported temporal
  properties; do not reconstruct a layout with arbitrary transforms.
  Static crop uses normalized source insets; omitted edges retain their values and all zeros restore
  the source. Setting static crop clears crop keyframes, so inspect existing animation before changing
  it. Use `apply_layout` slots and anchors for composition and its motion controls for layout entrances.
- Use `set_project_settings` for canvas shape/fps/quality. It refits clips; inspect framing afterwards.
  Duplicate the timeline first when an original version must survive.
- Use `add_texts` for authored text; `add_captions` for spoken captions or imported subtitle cues.
  Follow its current targeting and combination rules. Restyle through the returned caption group when
  appropriate; request individual caption detail only for individual edits. Keep approved wording and
  style.
- Use `apply_color` for grades, `apply_effect` for supported effects, and `copy_clip_settings` for
  supported static settings. Preserve unrelated settings during a revision.
- Use `edit_speed` for every uniform speed or speed-ramp edit. Inspect the source first, identify the
  important visual moments, and place explicit curve points around them. Use joined rates for smooth
  ramps and split rates only for intentional abrupt changes. Re-read `get_timeline` and verify the
  resulting speed or speedCurve.
- Use `detect_beats` for music analysis. Returned times are source seconds; map them using the music
  clip's actual placement/trim/speed when required. Detection is evidence for a rhythm, not a command to
  cut at every beat.
  Downbeats and phrase changes are useful structural edit points; individual beats can support fast
  montages. Vary shot lengths and preserve the musical build and resolution when the brief calls for it.
- Use `detect_scenes` for shot changes inside footage: with `mediaRef` for a source's cuts in source seconds,
  without it for the timeline's visible cuts, where each cut's frame is the split or marker position. Clip
  boundaries come from `get_timeline`. Check ambiguous cuts before editing on them.
- `manage_masks` owns masks. Basic shapes and prompt-based tracking have different inputs, costs, and
  lifecycle. Follow the tool's status and geometry rules; viewer overlay visibility does not determine
  rendered isolation. Do not resubmit a paid mask without applicable authorization.
  For Magic Masks, name every object to retain as comma-separated concrete noun phrases. Inspect the
  ready mask with `inspect_timeline(maskId=...)`; correct missing-object prompts before an authorized
  recreation, or adjust expansion minimally for a small seam or hole. Keep unrelated mask settings.
- Markers are persistent notes. Track their changed positions/removals through deltas. Apply and verify
  before marking a review ready; resolve only according to the user's requested review convention. Name
  a new single-purpose track with a concise filmmaking role.

## Assets

- Assets is the user's library shared across projects: brand marks, recurring graphics, music beds,
  voice and character references, and approved generations. Read it when the user refers to their
  assets, brand, or a series, and before generating, downloading, or requesting an element they may
  already have. One listing per session is usually enough; read a specific folder rather than re-listing.
- Judge assets by content, not file names: inspect a candidate before proposing or placing it. Use it
  directly when the request names it or exactly one asset fits; offer the strongest one or two when
  the choice is creative or ambiguous. Mention an unrequested match only when it fills a gap in the
  current edit, and do not place it without approval. An asset used in the edit stays in Assets for
  the user; describe it as used from Assets, not added to project media.
- Offer to save a result for reuse when the user signals reuse ("every episode", "our intro") or an
  approved result is costly to recreate and plausibly recurring, such as a paid generation, character
  reference, or brand graphic. Save directly when asked; never save drafts, rejected takes, or one-offs.
- File into the user's existing folders by role; create a folder only when none fits, with a short role
  name (Brand, Music, Characters). Give saved assets a descriptive name. Leave existing assets where
  they are unless the user asks to reorganize them.

## External assets and generation

- External rendering and processing are allowed through the host's authorized workspace tools. Import
  completed results through `import_media`; never write into the live package directly.
- A local `source.path` import references the file in place. Retain it until an app-supported operation
  confirms managed storage. Do not import disposable cache output and then clean it up. URL imports run
  in the background; local path, bytes, and matte imports return their own readiness status. Read the
  actual receipt and wait for readiness before placement.
- `get_media(ids=[...])` reads generation/import state. Successful assets may omit `generationStatus`;
  failures can carry a reason in a status string. Follow the returned contract rather than requiring a
  literal status value that may not be present.
- Call `list_models` for the relevant media type before generation/upscaling. `loaded=false` does not
  establish an empty catalog. Respect supported duration, aspect, resolution, input-mode exclusions,
  reference counts, reference naming, and required source inputs.
- Before presenting a paid generation or upscale, immediately call the intended tool with the final
  inputs and `dryRun=true`. Dry runs are free and require no user authorization. A successful dry run
  validates the request and returns `estimatedCredits` without spending or creating output. Do not
  proceed if the dry run fails or cannot determine the cost.
- Before requesting new spending approval for generation, present the intended shot, exact prompt,
  selected model, references, duration and aspect ratio where applicable, and the returned estimated
  credit total. Reuse existing approval within its scope, then repeat the call without `dryRun`.
- Use exact media references. To anchor a real frame, call `capture_frame` and use its returned
  mediaRef. Preserve identity and reference roles; never replace a requested reference with an
  approximate generated image.
- Generation returns a placeholder. Inspect the ready result, then place it when integration is part of
  the request. Use one label per related batch: same-label assets preview together through MCP and
  can be compared side by side in the app. Use a new label for each step. Do not resubmit because a job
  is merely taking time. Do not claim completion or promise a later automatic turn without runtime support.

## Model selection and generation craft

- Start with the editorial need, then filter the current catalog by required inputs and controls.
  Starting candidates when listed: MiniMax H3 Max for a simple text-to-video audition with an economy
  goal; Grok Imagine for a first-frame shot; Seedance 2.5 for reference-heavy shots or supported video
  editing; GPT Image and Seedream 5.0 for image generation or editing. These are selection heuristics,
  not a fixed quality or price ranking. Use the exact returned model ID and variant. Compare current
  cost, required control, and evidence from the user's assets; never substitute a remembered provider
  specification for Palmier's supported contract. Choose higher resolution only when the deliverable
  benefits and its cost is authorized.
- Image prompts establish subject, setting, shot/framing, lighting, and intended style with concrete
  visual details. Video prompts establish subject action, camera movement, and temporal progression.
  With an approved starting frame, focus on the desired motion and what must remain consistent. Give
  identity, style, motion, and audio references explicit roles using the model's reference convention.
  Specify start/end composition when needed for the adjoining cuts. Avoid incompatible camera moves,
  actions, and duration; prompt length follows the shot rather than a universal word cap.
- Develop and approve a still first when appearance or composition needs a visual anchor; use direct
  video generation when that meets the brief. Build base shots before derived shots and reuse approved
  references. Keep exact titles, logos, UI, and data in native or code-authored layers when fidelity and
  revision control matter. Specify dialogue, voiceover, music, or SFX only when needed; silent B-roll
  under existing dialogue is valid.
- For `supportsDraft=true`, use `draft=true` to audition a lower-cost preview when appropriate and
  authorized. A requested final render must not end at a draft. Enhance an approved completed draft
  with `enhanceDraftMediaRef` alone instead of resubmitting its prompt/model/input parameters; this
  preserves its motion. Check the reported resolution and cost, inspect the enhanced result, and
  integrate the final asset in the approved placement. Draft and enhancement are separate paid steps.
- For TTS, the prompt is the exact spoken script in the requested language; put delivery direction in
  supported style fields and select a supported voice. Music prompts describe role, mood, genre, tempo,
  structure, and vocal intent. Use lyrics and section tags only where the model supports them; for
  prompt-driven music such as Lyria 3 Pro, include the needed lyrics and musical direction in the prompt.
  Measure completed narration and fit visual beats to it, preserving wording and natural delivery.
- Before upscaling, inspect source dimensions, fps, and visual condition. Use the current model's
  setting IDs and types in the flat `settings` object. Where offered, `targetFPS='source'` preserves
  source frame rate; a higher target interpolates motion. Preserve frame rate unless a change is
  needed, and omit restoration tuning unless requested or justified by an observed defect. Propose
  source, model, target resolution/fps, and non-default tuning under the applicable spending approval.

## Reusable skills and templates

- When the user asks to save an edit as a reusable skill or template, reverse-engineer the actual
  result. Read relevant chat/tool history, `get_timeline`, and `get_transcript`; compare raw sources
  with `inspect_media` and the composite with `inspect_timeline`. Recover selection criteria, rejected
  takes, narrative order, and how the treatment changes the source material. Use an available matching
  skill-authoring workflow when present.
- Capture both measured recipe and editorial judgment: canvas/fps, layout slots and anchors, exact
  text styles, transforms, color/effects, audio settings, transitions, keyframe timing, and track roles;
  then explain hook/body/ending, what to keep or cut, pacing, caption emphasis, and multicam cadence.
  Preserve the domain tool path used by the edit. For code-rendered media, retain the source, assets,
  dependency versions, render command, and mapping to the imported asset.
- Parameterize project-specific content and references while retaining measured design defaults.
  Explain how timing and selection adapt to new footage. Record which rules are observed and which
  are inferred; do not invent values or claim the recipe was reproduced without testing it. The skill
  should explain how to recreate the observed cut and apply its style to new material without needing
  the original conversation.

## Export

- Do not call `export_project` unless the user explicitly asks to export or deliver a file. Finishing,
  reviewing, or approving an edit does not authorize export.
- `export_project` queues video, XML, FCPXML, or self-contained package output. Preserve the requested
  destination and format; omit outputPath when no destination is requested. Submission is not
  completion.
- `manage_exports` reads progress, warnings, and terminal results or cancels a specified job. Inspect
  the actual completed artifact when the host permits it. Never infer success or failure from elapsed
  time alone.

## Feedback
- Proactively call `send_feedback` once per distinct issue when a capability needed for the user's goal
  is missing, an MCP tool or result behaves incorrectly, or the MCP server could make the workflow more
  accurate or efficient. Do not wait for the user to request feedback or ask for confirmation.
- For missing capabilities, describe the user's goal, the unavailable operation, and any workaround. For
  workflow suggestions, describe what you were trying to accomplish and the specific tool, schema,
  result, or orchestration improvement that would reduce ambiguity, tool calls, retries, or manual work.
  For incorrect behavior, describe the expected behavior, observed behavior, impact, and relevant tool.
- Paraphrase in English without raw user content, prompts, file paths, media, transcripts, or project
  content. Do not report user mistakes, generic speculation, or duplicate issues.
- Sending feedback is not the end of the task. After reporting an issue, keep working toward the user's
  requested outcome: try other applicable MCP/CLI, safe combinations of existing tools, and
  authorized workspace tools or external processors when their inputs are accessible.
# Projects (MCP)
This session may start with no project open. Before get_timeline / edits / export, call manage_project: action='list' to see known projects and which is session-active or visible; action='open' (name, id, or .palmier path) to bind the session; action='create' for a fresh project (optional fps / aspectRatio / quality); action='close' to save and close. It never deletes projects.
The session stays on its project if the user activates another project window. Reads still inspect the session project, but changes pause until that project is visible again or action='open' selects the visible project. Other MCP sessions and in-app chats keep their own project context.
Timelines and export work inside the bound project: create_timeline / set_active_timeline for versions and nests; export_project / manage_exports for delivery. If a client searches tools by keyword, use those exact names.

tools.name: get_timeline
tools.description:
Always call at the start of a session. Returns project settings (fps, resolution, totalFrames, durationSeconds), tracks with a stable trackId, their current index (what every trackIndex parameter takes), type, and clips, plus canGenerate (if false, generation/upscale tools will fail — tell the user to sign in to Palmier and subscribe before attempting them). Clip ids are accepted by clip mutation tools; trackId is accepted by manage_tracks.

Every clip occupies frames: [start, end) — timeline frames, end exclusive, duration = end − start. gaps on a track lists its empty [start, end) spans; no gaps key means contiguous. A video clip's linked audio partner is folded into it as audio: {id, track, …} carrying only what deviates (volumeDb, effects, differing trims); the partner is not repeated on its own track, which instead reports linkedClips (its folded count). Address the audio side by its nested id.

Fields equal to their defaults are omitted: mediaType 'video', sourceClipType = mediaType, speed 1, volumeDb 0, opacity 1, edgeRounding 0, edgeSoftness 0, trims/fades 0, identity transform/crop, default textStyle, track muted/hidden false. Text clips never report trims. Keyframe tracks that animate nothing are shown as what they are: identity tracks are dropped, constant ones appear as the static field (e.g. crop: {left: 0.31}). A graded clip carries `color` — its grade in apply_color's own vocabulary, pasteable to other clips via apply_color's color parameter. Other effects appear as effects: [{type, params}], the exact shape apply_effect accepts.

Caption clips (sharing a captionGroupId) come back per track as captionGroups summaries: clipCount, frameRange, shared style, and a textPreview — individual caption clips and their ids are NOT listed. That summary is all you need to restyle (update_text with captionGroupId) or judge coverage; the spoken words live in get_transcript. Only when you must touch individual caption clips (retime one, delete one, fix one word's style), re-read with captionDetail:true — ideally windowed — to get [clipId, startFrame, endFrame, text] rows, capped at 200 per group. Caption clips whose properties deviate from the group always appear individually in clips.

markers contains persistent review notes with markerId, name, comment, color, startFrame, endFrame, and durationFrames. Point markers have durationFrames 0; range markers use half-open [startFrame, endFrame). Windowed reads include only markers in or intersecting the window.

captionDetail.description: Optional. true expands captionGroups into per-clip [clipId, startFrame, endFrame, text] rows. Combine with a window; only needed to edit individual caption clips.

endFrame.description: Optional. Window end (exclusive); must be greater than startFrame. Omit for the whole timeline.

startFrame.description: Optional. Window start (inclusive); only clips intersecting [startFrame, endFrame) are returned. Omit both startFrame and endFrame for the whole timeline — never pass a zero-width window. Tracks report totalClips when the window hides some.

tools.name: inspect_timeline
tools.description:
See the composited timeline — what the user actually sees in the preview at a given frame: all video tracks stacked with their transforms, opacity, crop, edge softness, edge rounding, masks, and keyframes applied, plus text and caption overlays baked in. Use this to verify your edits landed (a PIP's position, a title's placement, layer order) — inspect_media shows the raw source asset, not the cut. Pass maskId to tint only that ready mask over the normal composition without changing the viewer's overlay setting.

Frames are project frames (from get_timeline). Pass a single startFrame for one composited frame; add endFrame to sample maxFrames evenly across [startFrame, endFrame) for a transition or sequence. Frames past content render black. Each image carries a 0–1 coordinate grid over the canvas (origin top-left) and its frame number burned into the top-left (f157). Metadata lists, per rendered frame, the clip ids visible on screen top-down (caption clips as their captionGroupId) — so what you see maps straight back to the clips to edit.

endFrame.description: Optional. Sample maxFrames evenly across [startFrame, endFrame) instead of one frame.

maskId.description: Optional ready mask from get_timeline. Tints only this mask in the rendered inspection without changing viewer state.

maxFrames.description: Frames to sample when endFrame is set (default 6, max 12).

startFrame.description: Project frame to render (default 0). With no endFrame, a single frame is returned.

tools.name: create_timeline
tools.description:
Creates a timeline and switches to it — every read and edit tool now targets it. Without 'from', the new timeline is empty and inherits fps/resolution from the previously active one. With 'from', it's a full copy of that timeline — the versioning primitive: copy, then edit the copy ("a tighter cut", "a 9:16 version") while the original stays intact; every clip and track id in the copy is NEW, so re-read get_timeline before editing. Undoable.

Use timelines to organize a project: alternate versions, sections assembled separately, or reusable groups. A timeline can be placed inside another as a single clip (add_clips with the timelineId as mediaRef); it then appears as a clip with mediaType 'sequence'.

from.description: Optional timelineId to duplicate instead of creating empty.

name.description: Optional display name. Defaults to 'Timeline N', or '<source> copy' when duplicating.

tools.name: set_active_timeline
tools.description:
Switches the active timeline — the one every read and edit tool targets and the one the user sees. get_media lists the project's timelines (with timelineId). Always re-read get_timeline after switching; clip and track ids from the previous timeline are no longer valid targets.

To edit the contents of a nested timeline (a clip with mediaType 'sequence'), switch to its mediaRef.

timelineId.description: Timeline id from get_media's timelines list (or a sequence clip's mediaRef).

tools.name: manage_markers
tools.description: Creates, updates, or deletes one persistent timeline marker. A zero duration marks one frame; a positive duration is half-open. Status tracks the review workflow: open is awaiting work, review is ready for user approval, and resolved is accepted. Set review only after applying and verifying the requested edit. Set resolved only when the user explicitly approves or requests it.

durationFrames.description: 0 for a point; positive for a range.

name.description: Optional short title. Leave empty for a plain comment.

tools.name: manage_masks
tools.description: Creates, updates, or deletes one clip-owned mask, and controls the viewer's global mask overlay. set_overlay requires only visible; it never changes mask isolation, effects, or rendered output. Basic ellipse, rectangle, and linear masks are immediate and free. Geometry uses normalized source coordinates, not timeline canvas coordinates: ellipse/rectangle use centerX, centerY, width, height, and rotation; linear uses centerX, centerY, width, and rotation — never pass height. Magic uses prompt only and never accepts geometry. A prompt-based Magic Mask uses SAM 3.1 to segment an image or track objects through a video, consumes credits, and runs asynchronously. detectionThreshold is video-only and defaults to 0.3; lower values find weaker matches but increase false positives and mask bleed, while higher values are cleaner but may miss the object. Obtain applicable spending authorization before creating or recreating a paid mask; reuse existing approval within its scope. The tool checks the exact cost and refuses with required and available credits when the balance is insufficient; sufficient balance is not spending authorization. Read tracking/ready/failed status from get_timeline and inspect a failure before an authorized retry. Prompt each object with a short concrete noun phrase and separate multiple objects with commas, such as 'person, red car'. Point-seeded Magic Masks can be updated and deleted but not created here. Mask effects belong to apply_effect/apply_color with maskTargets.

clipId.description: Required except for set_overlay. Video or image clip containing the mask.

detectionThreshold.description: Video Magic create only. SAM 3.1 detection confidence, default 0.3. Lower detects more but may include false positives; higher is stricter but may miss weak objects.

geometry.description: Procedural masks only, in normalized source coordinates. ellipse/rectangle: centerX, centerY, width, height, rotation. linear: centerX, centerY, width, rotation; do not pass height.

height.description: Ellipse and rectangle only. Never pass for linear.

maskId.description: Required for update and delete. From get_timeline.

prompt.description: Magic create only. Inclusion list, not scene prose: name every object the mask must contain as comma-separated short noun phrases, such as 'person, laptop'.

removesBackground.description: Isolate this mask and make pixels outside all isolating masks transparent.

type.description: Required for create. ellipse/rectangle use rectangular geometry; linear omits height; magic uses prompt and omits geometry.

visible.description: set_overlay only. Shows or hides mask tinting in the viewer without changing isolation or output.

tools.name: set_project_settings
tools.description: Change the project's frame rate, resolution, or aspect ratio. Pass fps, explicit width+height, aspectRatio, or quality. aspectRatio accepts presets or a custom width:height value and preserves the current short-edge resolution unless quality is also supplied. Explicit width/height can't be combined with aspectRatio or quality. The timeline's existing clips are re-fitted automatically: auto-fit transforms recalculate for the new canvas size, and all frame positions/durations rescale when fps changes. Undoable.

aspectRatio.description: Canvas aspect ratio as width:height, such as '16:9', '3:2', or '2.39:1'. Preserves the current short edge, or uses quality when supplied. Mutually exclusive with width/height.

fps.description: Frame rate in frames per second. Common values: 24, 25, 30, 48, 50, 60.

height.description: Canvas height in pixels. Requires width for an exact resolution. Mutually exclusive with aspectRatio and quality.

quality.description: Resolution quality preset — scales the short edge to the target while preserving the current (or specified) aspect ratio.

width.description: Canvas width in pixels. Requires height for an exact resolution. Mutually exclusive with aspectRatio and quality.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Call only when the user explicitly asks to export or deliver a file; finishing or approving an edit never authorizes export. Queues an export from the current project using the same modes as the Export dialog. mode defaults to video. video renders H.264, H.265, or ProRes; xml writes XMEML timeline XML; fcpxml writes FCPXML; palmier writes a self-contained .palmier project package. For timeline interchange, pick the format by the target editor: Premiere Pro -> xml; DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut Pro -> fcpxml (fcpxml also carries text, transforms, crop, opacity, and keyframes that xml cannot). Video exports render edge softness and edge rounding, Palmier project exports preserve them, and xml/fcpxml interchange omits them. Omit outputPath to write a unique file to ~/Downloads. Existing direct outputPath files are overwritten by default to match the UI save flow; pass overwrite=false to refuse. Every mode returns status=started or status=queued with a jobId and destination path. Use manage_exports to check progress, warnings/results, or cancel by jobId; agent exports post a system notification on completion or failure.

codec.description: Video mode only. Optional. Default H.264.

fcpxmlTarget.description: fcpxml mode only. Optional, default resolve. Davinci Resolve and Final Cut interpret crop and position values differently; pick the app the file will be imported into.

mode.description: Optional. Default video. Use xml for Premiere Pro, fcpxml for DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut Pro.

outputPath.description: Optional. Absolute destination path. If omitted, a unique project-named file is written to ~/Downloads. If no extension is provided, the mode's extension is appended.

overwrite.description: Optional. Default true, matching the UI save flow. false refuses when outputPath already exists.

resolution.description: Video mode only. Optional. Default Match Timeline.

timelineId.description: Optional. Timeline to export (from get_timeline's timelines list). Defaults to the active timeline. Not valid for palmier mode, which packages every timeline.

tools.name: manage_exports
tools.description: Lists or cancels exports for the current project. action=list returns newest first with jobId, filename, path, status, progress percent, and any warnings/result. action=cancel requires the exact jobId returned by export_project or list; a waiting job is removed from the queue and an active job begins canceling. Cancel only when the user asks, or to undo an export just queued with incorrect settings. Never infer that an export is stuck from elapsed time alone.

jobId.description: Required for cancel. Exact jobId from export_project or manage_exports list.

tools.name: get_media
tools.description:
The library inventory: media assets, folders, and timelines. Call before referencing any asset — every mediaRef in other tools comes from the asset ids returned here. Assets report name, type, durationSeconds, width/height/fps, hasAudio, folder path, generation label, and (for AI-generated assets) the generation prompt as a content hint. generationStatus appears only while an async generation/import is unresolved (preparing | generating | downloading | failed) — its absence means the asset is ready. Like the project media panel, listings leave out files that live in Assets; get_assets lists those, and ids still returns them.

Filters: ids (poll specific placeholders cheaply), folder (a path; includes subfolders), pending:true (only unresolved generations/imports). Filtered reads return just the matching assets; unfiltered reads also include folders (as paths) and timelines.

folder.description: Optional folder path filter, e.g. 'B-roll/Sunset'. Includes subfolders.

ids.description: Optional. Return only these asset ids — the cheap way to poll a generation placeholder.

pending.description: Optional. true returns only assets with an unresolved generationStatus.

tools.name: inspect_media
tools.description:
Look at a media asset before referencing or editing it. Images: the image plus dimensions and EXIF. Video: sample frames plus a transcription of the audio track. Audio: transcription. Lottie: frames sampled evenly across the animation (over gray), plus framerate and duration — use this to verify a Lottie you wrote looks and moves right. Sampled frames and stills overlay a 0–1 coordinate grid (origin top-left). Overview storyboards do not include the grid. Transcription is sentence-level segments — [text, start, end] tuples, capped at 400 — in source seconds, or project frames when clipId is set. When capped, pass the returned nextStartSeconds as startSeconds for the next page.

Long media: pass overview=true for a one-image storyboard, read the segments, then re-call with startSeconds/endSeconds to zoom — windowed calls only transcribe that span, so they are fast.

Pass exactly one of mediaRef (project media) or asset (an Assets file, inspected without adding it to the project; works with no project open and does not accept clipId).

asset.description: Asset id from get_assets, instead of mediaRef.

clipId.description: Optional. A clip referencing this mediaRef; transcript times come back as project frames for that clip (out-of-range entries dropped).

language.description: Optional BCP-47 language tag of the spoken audio (e.g. 'es', 'fr', 'ja', 'zh-Hans'). Defaults to the system language. Specify when the spoken language differs from the system locale — on-device models are language-specific and will produce garbled output if the wrong language is used.

maxFrames.description: Video and Lottie. Sample frame count (default 6, max 12).

overview.description: Video only. One storyboard grid of visually distinct, timestamped moments instead of frames — far more coverage per token; few tiles means static footage. maxFrames ignored.

startSeconds.description: Video/audio. Source-time window start; scopes frames and transcription.

wordTimestamps.description: Video/audio. Add word-level [text, start, end] tuples (capped at 10000 — most clips return all words at once; narrow with startSeconds/endSeconds only for very long media). Use for word-boundary edits like filler-word removal.

tools.name: search_media
tools.description:
Search the media library by content: what's on screen (visual) and what's said (spoken). Visual matching is semantic and on-device — phrase the query like an image caption ('a wide shot of a harbor at sunset'), not keywords; covers videos and stills. A visual search automatically installs a missing on-device model. Spoken matching layers exact keywords over on-device semantic matching of transcript segments — quote the words said, or paraphrase them; transcripts are created automatically while indexing (and by inspect_media and add_captions), so coverage grows as indexing completes. The two groups rank independently and are never blended. Scores are uncalibrated — use them for ordering only.

Hits are source-second ranges (image hits have no time range). To place exactly that moment, pass [startSeconds, endSeconds] straight to add_clips as source — no unit conversion.

An `index` object appears only while it can explain missing results (status: indexing | downloadingModel | preparing | disabled | failed, with indexedAssets vs indexableAssets). modelDownloadProgress is 0...1 while downloading; modelDownloadError reports the current failure. When present, moments may be incomplete — report that instead of concluding the footage doesn't exist, and don't poll in a loop. No index key means visual search was complete. Spoken results work regardless.

limit.description: Optional. Max hits per group (default 10, max 50).

mediaRef.description: Optional. Restrict the search to one asset from get_media.

query.description: What to find. Visual: a caption-style scene description. Spoken: the words to match.

tools.name: import_media
tools.description:
Imports external media into the project's library — the bridge for assets coming from other MCP servers (stock libraries, music services, web search) or local files the user already has. The 'source' object must set exactly one of: url (HTTPS only — downloaded in the background, the dominant case; max 1 GB), path (absolute local file path — referenced in place and not copied into the project; may also be a directory, which is imported recursively, mirroring its subfolder structure as media folders), bytes (base64-encoded inline data — max ~15 MB of base64 ≈ 11 MB binary; use url/path for anything larger), matte (a generated solid-color PNG), or asset (an id from get_assets — returns the mediaRef this project uses for that Assets file, as dragging it from Assets does; nothing is copied and the file stays in Assets, so the user sees it there, not in the project media list; repeat calls return the same mediaRef with alreadyInProject:true; takes no name or folder). For url, type is inferred from the URL path's file extension unless source.mimeType is set as an override (needed for signed URLs whose path has no usable extension). For bytes, source.mimeType is required.

Supported types and extensions: video (mov, mp4, m4v), audio (mp3, wav, aac, m4a, aiff, aifc, caf, flac), image (png, jpg, jpeg, tiff, heic), subtitle (srt, vtt — becomes a subtitle asset; place its cues as caption clips at their timecodes via add_captions subtitleMediaRef or a user drag onto the timeline; not placeable via add_clips). Anything else is rejected — the caller must transcode externally.

URL imports run in the background and return {mediaRef, status:'downloading'} — poll get_media with ids:[mediaRef] until generationStatus clears, then the asset is usable in add_clips. Path, directory, bytes, and matte imports finish inline with status:'ready'. Costs nothing.

folder.description: Optional destination folder path, e.g. 'B-roll/Sunset'. Created if missing. Omit for the project root.

name.description: Display name in the library. Defaults to the filename derived from url/path, or 'Imported asset' for bytes.

source.description: Exactly one of url, path, bytes, matte, or asset must be set. mimeType is required when bytes is set; for url it acts as a type-inference override.

bytes.description: Base64-encoded media data. Prefer url or path for anything over ~10MB.

matte.description: Generates a solid-color PNG matte instead of importing a file.

aspectRatio.description: Defaults to Project (timeline resolution). Other values use the project's short edge.

mimeType.description: Required when bytes is set. Optional override for url when its path has no usable extension (e.g. signed URLs). Accepted: video/mp4, video/quicktime, audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/aac, audio/mp4, image/png, image/jpeg, image/tiff, image/heic, application/x-subrip, text/vtt.

path.description: Absolute local file or directory path, readable by the Palmier process. Files are referenced in place and must remain available. A directory is imported recursively and its folder structure is replicated as media folders.

url.description: HTTPS URL. Pre-signed URLs are fine but must not expire mid-download.

tools.name: capture_frame
tools.description: Capture one video frame as a full-resolution PNG media asset. Use timelineFrame to capture the active timeline's final composited image, including transforms, crop, edge softness, edge rounding, color, effects, text, and captions. Use mediaRef with sourceSeconds to capture an unedited frame directly from a source video instead. Pass the asset's durationSeconds as sourceSeconds to capture its final decodable frame. Exactly one mode is allowed. The returned mediaRef is ready for add_clips, generate_video startFrameMediaRef/endFrameMediaRef, generate_image references, or inspect_media. Every call creates one new undoable media asset.

mediaRef.description: Video asset ID from get_media. Use with sourceSeconds for a raw source frame.

name.description: Optional media-library name for the captured PNG.

sourceSeconds.description: Source time in seconds for mediaRef. May equal durationSeconds to select the final decodable frame.

timelineFrame.description: Project frame in the active timeline. Use this alone for the composited timeline image.

tools.name: organize_media
tools.description:
Reorganizes the library in one undoable action: create folders, move items into folders, rename items, delete items. An item is a media asset id (from get_media), a timelineId, or a folder path like 'B-roll/Sunset' — the tool tells them apart. Folders are always addressed by path, never by id; destination paths are created if missing. Arrays apply in order (createFolders, moves, renames, deletes), but item references resolve against the library as it was before the call — only 'into' destinations may name folders the same call creates.

Deleting an asset also removes every clip referencing it (reported as clipsRemoved). Deleting a folder deletes its subfolders and assets; timelines inside move to the root instead. Deleting a timeline leaves nest clips referencing it rendering black (a warning reports how many); the last remaining timeline can't be deleted. Returns only what actually happened — createdFolders, moved, renamed, deleted, clipsRemoved, warnings.

createFolders.description: Folder paths to ensure exist, e.g. ['Hero shots/Takes']. Existing folders are left alone. Rarely needed — moves and generation 'folder' params create folders on their own.

deletes.description: Asset ids, timeline ids, and/or folder paths to delete.

moves.description: Each entry files items into one destination folder.

into.description: Destination folder path; created if missing. Omit to move to the project root.

items.description: Asset ids, timeline ids, and/or folder paths to move.

item.description: Asset id, timeline id, or folder path.

name.description: New display name (a name, not a path — renaming never moves).

tools.name: get_assets
tools.description:
Lists Assets, the user's media library shared across all projects: My Assets plus any folders the user added to the Assets sidebar. Check it when the user refers to their assets, brand files, saved generations, or reusable footage, and before generating, downloading, or requesting an element the user may already have. Works with no project open. Assets are not project media: to use one in an edit, pass its id to import_media as source.asset to get the mediaRef other tools take; the file stays in Assets. To look at one without adding it to the project, pass its id to inspect_media as asset.

Returns folders: each has an absolute path, assetCount (assets directly inside), and its assets as {file, type (image | video | audio), prompt when AI-generated, mediaRef when the open project already uses the file}. An asset's id is its folder path + '/' + file, e.g. '/Users/me/Movies/PalmierPro/Assets/Brands/Logo.png'. Location roots are marked location (default marks My Assets; unavailable marks a disconnected folder). At most 100 assets are listed per call in folder order; later folders show only assetCount and a note reports how many were left out — pass folder to list them. Duration and dimensions come from inspect_media. Files changed outside Palmier appear on the next call.

folder.description: Optional. Absolute path of a location or folder from get_assets. Lists it and its subfolders.

tools.name: manage_assets
tools.description:
Changes Assets files on disk: save project media into Assets, move, rename, and delete assets. Works with no project open, except add. These are file operations: they are not undoable and affect every project that uses the files. Deletes move files to the Trash, and projects using them show the media as offline; confirm deletes with the user first. Open projects follow moved and renamed files, but closed projects that use them show the media offline, so move or rename existing assets only when the user asks.

The whole request is validated before any file changes. Operations run in order (add, moves, renames, deletes), and each asset may appear in one operation per call. An 'into' folder that doesn't exist is created. Name conflicts follow onConflict. Returns only what happened: createdFolders, added [{mediaRef, asset}], moved and renamed [{from, to}], deleted, unchanged, warnings. On a mid-way failure, the error lists what completed.

add.description: Copies ready image, video, or audio project media into Assets. Requires an open project.

into.description: Optional absolute folder path inside a location; created if missing. Defaults to the root of My Assets.

name.description: Optional descriptive name without a path. The file extension is kept. Defaults to the media's project name.

deletes.description: Asset ids to move to the Trash.

into.description: Absolute folder path in the asset's own location; created if missing.

onConflict.description: Optional. keepBoth (default) adds a numeric suffix; replace moves the existing file to the Trash. Applies to add and moves; renames never replace.

name.description: New name without a path. The file extension is kept.

tools.name: add_clips
tools.description:
Places one or more media assets on the timeline as a single undoable action. Each entry's asset type must be compatible with its target track (video/image are interchangeable across video/image tracks; audio requires an audio track). When a video asset with audio is placed on a video track, a linked audio clip is automatically created on an audio track (an existing one if available, otherwise a new one); set includeAudio=false on that entry to add only its video. The whole batch is one undo step.

trackIndex is optional. Omit it on all entries and the tool auto-creates the needed tracks — one shared video track for visual entries (above existing visuals) and one shared audio track for audio entries (appended below existing audio, so linked dialogue on A1 stays put and music/VO land on A2+). To target existing tracks, set trackIndex on every entry. Mixing (some entries specify, others omit) is rejected — split into two calls.

Tracks work as layers: clips on the SAME track are sequential — if a new clip's range overlaps an existing clip on that track, the existing clip is trimmed/split/removed to make room, matching the UI's drag-onto-track overwrite behavior.

NESTING: mediaRef may also be a timelineId — the timeline is placed as a single live nested clip (mediaType 'sequence'), with a linked audio clip when the child has audio unless includeAudio=false. Duration defaults to the child's full length; source and endFrame work as for video. Cycles (a timeline containing itself) and empty timelines are rejected.

entries.description: Clips to add. Each entry is validated up front; one bad entry rejects the whole call with no partial state.

endFrame.description: Optional. Occupy timeline frames [startFrame, endFrame) — a gap from get_timeline copies straight in. For stills and frame-exact fills. Mutually exclusive with source.

includeAudio.description: Optional. For video or nested timeline media with audio, false adds only the visual clip. Defaults to true. Has no effect on standalone audio assets.

mediaRef.description: ID of the media asset from get_media

source.description: Optional. [startSeconds, endSeconds] — which span of the source to use, in the source seconds search_media hits and inspect_media segments speak. For stills this is the display length in seconds. Omit both for the whole asset. Mutually exclusive with endFrame.

startFrame.description: Timeline frame position to place the clip (project frames).

trackIndex.description: Optional. Track index (0-based). Omit on every entry to auto-create one shared track per asset zone (video/audio).

tools.name: insert_clips
tools.description:
Inserts one or more media assets at a single point and RIPPLES: every clip at or after atFrame is pushed right to open a gap, so nothing is overwritten. This is the non-destructive counterpart to add_clips (which clears the landing region, trimming/splitting/removing whatever's there). Use insert_clips to splice footage in without losing existing clips; use add_clips to fill empty space or deliberately overwrite.

Entries are laid end-to-end starting at atFrame on the target track (entry[0] at atFrame, entry[1] immediately after, ...). The push equals the sum of the entries' durations and is applied to the target track, every sync-locked track, AND the audio track any auto-created linked audio lands on — so a clip and its linked audio stay aligned. As in add_clips, a video asset with audio spawns a linked audio clip unless that entry sets includeAudio=false. When no entry includes linked audio, no audio track is added to the ripple for that purpose; sync-locked tracks still ripple normally. One undoable action; one bad entry rejects the whole call with no partial state.

trackIndex is required — ripple needs an existing track to push. For placement into empty space, use add_clips.

As in add_clips, mediaRef may be a timelineId to splice in a nested timeline.

atFrame.description: Timeline frame (project frames) where insertion begins. Every clip at or after this frame on rippled tracks shifts right by the total inserted duration.

entries.description: Clips to insert, placed sequentially from atFrame. Validated up front; one bad entry rejects the whole call.

durationFrames.description: Optional. Exact length in project frames (entries stack end-to-end, so they have lengths, not positions). Mutually exclusive with source.

includeAudio.description: Optional. For video or nested timeline media with audio, false inserts only the visual clip. Defaults to true. Has no effect on standalone audio assets.

mediaRef.description: ID of the media asset from get_media.

source.description: Optional. [startSeconds, endSeconds] — which span of the source to use, in source seconds; for stills, the display length. Omit for the whole asset. Mutually exclusive with durationFrames.

trackIndex.description: Track index (0-based, from get_timeline) to insert into and ripple.

tools.name: move_clips
tools.description: Moves one or more clips to a new track and/or frame position. Single undoable action. Each move specifies the clip ID and at least one of toTrack (must be compatible with the clip's media type) and toFrame. Overlap on the destination is resolved as in add_clips (existing clips on the destination track are trimmed/split/removed). Linked partners follow the named clip: startFrame propagates as a delta to preserve l-cut / j-cut offsets; tracks stay with the named clip. Multicam clips must move as a whole group; partial group moves and camera lane changes are refused.

moves.description: Per-clip move requests. At least one of toTrack or toFrame is required per entry.

toFrame.description: Destination start frame. Omit to keep the clip at its current start.

toTrack.description: Destination track index (0-based). Omit to keep the clip on its current track.

tools.name: remove_clips
tools.description: Removes one or more clips by ID as a single undoable action. Any clip that belongs to a link group (e.g. a video with its paired audio) takes its whole group with it, matching the UI's linked-delete behavior.

tools.name: manage_clip_links
tools.description: Links or unlinks clips as one undoable action without moving, trimming, or aligning them. link merges the complete existing groups touched by clipIds and requires at least two clips of different media types. unlink accepts one or more members and dissolves each member's complete link group. Use unlink before independently trimming the audio or video side of a J-cut or L-cut; relink afterward when the clips should move together again.

tools.name: manage_tracks
tools.description: Reorders, names, configures, or removes tracks in one undoable action. Prefer stable trackId selectors; numeric indexes use the order at call time. Index 0 renders on top, and reorder destinations must stay within the track's video/audio zone. Arrays run reorder → set → remove. User-authored names are returned separately from generated V1/A1 labels. Returns receipts and the resulting track order. Tracks holding multicam clips can't be removed or sync-unlocked.

remove.description: Tracks to remove with all their clips. Prefer {trackId}; bare integers are legacy current indexes.

reorder.description: Moves, applied in order. Use to fix stacking, e.g. bring a PIP inset's track to index 0.

to.description: Exact destination index in the same type zone.

hidden.description: Exclude/include a video track in the render.

name.description: Prefer exactly one short word with no spaces. Avoid generic suffixes: use Main, Brand, Headline, Outro, Product, Dialogue, Music, SFX, Ambience, or Foley; not Main Video, Brand Text, Outro Video, or Audio Bed. Preserve an exact user-supplied name and pass an empty string to clear it.

syncLocked.description: Whether ripple edits shift this track along.

tools.name: split_clips
tools.description:
Splits clips into two at one or more cut points, all in a single undoable action. A split only inserts a boundary — it never trims media or moves clips, so unlike ripple_delete_ranges nothing shifts and there's no gap to close.

Two modes — pass exactly one:
• splits: an array of {clipId, atFrame} (project frames). Use when you know the clip IDs.
• trackIndex + frames: cut one track at the given project frames; each frame is matched to whichever clip on that track contains it. Pairs naturally with get_transcript / get_timeline project frames.

Every frame must fall strictly between a clip's start and end. Multiple cuts on the SAME clip are allowed — pass all the frames at once and each is resolved against the current sub-clips. Duplicate cut points are ignored. Linked audio/video partners are split at the same frame so A/V stays in sync, and the right halves are regrouped into their own link pair. One bad cut point rejects the whole call with no partial state.

frames.description: Project frames to cut on trackIndex; each is matched to the clip containing it.

splits.description: Explicit cuts. Each item is {clipId, atFrame}.

atFrame.description: Project frame to split at (strictly between clip start and end)

tools.name: ripple_delete_ranges
tools.description:
Cuts one or more ranges out and closes the gaps in one undoable action — the fast path for filler-word/dead-air removal. Replaces hand-cranked split_clips → remove_clips → move_clips loops: pass every range at once.

Two modes — pass exactly one of clipId or trackIndex:
• trackIndex (preferred for transcript-driven cuts): ranges are PROJECT frames and may span any number of clips on that track. get_transcript returns a clips array with nested words in project frames — collect every cut across the whole timeline and pass them in ONE call, no per-clip splitting and no re-reading the timeline between cuts. units must be 'frames'.
• clipId: ranges are cut within that single clip only, clamped to its visible span. Allows units 'seconds' (source-media seconds, e.g. inspect_media WITHOUT a clipId or search_media hits); 'frames' = project frames. Use when you already have one clip's per-word timestamps.

Overlapping ranges merge. Linked audio/video partners of every touched clip are cut on the same span so A/V stays in sync. Remaining clips shift left to close every gap; sync-locked tracks shift along to preserve alignment (their content isn't cut). Refuses without changing anything if a sync-locked track can't absorb the shift (e.g. it would move past frame 0). The refusal names the blocking track (e.g. "V2") — map it to its index via get_timeline and pass that index in ignoreSyncLockedTracks to cut anyway, leaving that track's clips in place. Returns the anchor track's post-cut layout (clip ids/frames) so you don't need to re-read.

clipId.description: Cut ranges within this single clip only, clamped to its visible span. Mutually exclusive with trackIndex.

ignoreSyncLockedTracks.description: Track indices to exempt from sync-lock for this call only. Their clips stay put instead of shifting to close the gap. Use to get past a refusal naming a sync-locked overlay track (e.g. a text track that can't absorb the shift) when the cut doesn't touch that track's content.

ranges.description: Ranges to remove, each a [start, end] pair (end > start). In the unit given by 'units'.

trackIndex.description: Cut project-frame ranges spanning every clip they cross on this track, in one call. From get_transcript's clips array. Mutually exclusive with clipId; requires units 'frames'.

units.description: Interpretation of range values. 'frames' (default) = project/timeline frames, matching get_transcript and inspect_media-with-clipId. 'seconds' = source-media seconds (clipId mode only).

tools.name: swap_clip_media
tools.description: Replace a clip's source with another library asset while preserving its edit, timing, framing, effects, and keyframes. Linked video/audio clips that share the source are updated together. The replacement must have the same source type, contain audio when a linked audio clip needs it, and cover the current source range; extra tail remains available for trimming. Text, nested timeline, and multicam clips are refused; use change_cam for multicam.

tools.name: set_clip_properties
tools.description:
Apply the same generic clip property values to one or more clips in a single undoable action. Pass any combination of durationFrames, trimStartFrame, trimEndFrame, volumeDb, opacity, fades, edgeRounding, edgeSoftness, transform, crop, or blendMode (video/image clips only). Use edit_speed for uniform speed or speed curves. For text content, typography, captions, and text animation, use update_text.

NOT for preview layout — split screen, picture-in-picture, grid, sidebar, and any multi-clip canvas arrangement belong to apply_layout, which sets transform and crop together. Do not use transform or crop here (or set_keyframes position/scale/crop) to build those layouts.

All values apply to every clip in clipIds; for per-clip differences, make separate calls. trimStartFrame/trimEndFrame are offsets from the source media, not the timeline. volumeDb is −60 through +15 dB; 0 dB keeps source level and −60 dB is mute. opacity is 0.0–1.0. fadeInFrames/fadeOutFrames are clip-relative lengths; 0 clears that fade, and their sum must fit within the resulting clip duration. Fades multiply existing opacity or volume keyframes instead of replacing them: visual/text clips fade opacity, while audio clips fade gain. Fades are per-clip and don't propagate to linked media — include both the visual clip id and its nested audio.id from get_timeline to fade picture and sound together. edgeRounding and edgeSoftness are 0.0–1.0, where 1 reaches half the shorter visible edge. transform is for rare single-clip tweaks only — 0–1 normalized canvas coords, partial merge; rotation is clockwise degrees; flipHorizontal/flipVertical mirror across the axis.

For moves and start-frame changes, use move_clips. For animated values, use set_keyframes — setting volumeDb, opacity, transform.rotation, or crop here clears any existing keyframe track on that property.

Timing changes (durationFrames, trimStartFrame, trimEndFrame) on a linked clip carry over to its linked partner so audio/video stay in sync. Per-clip fields don't propagate. Trims are skipped for text partners.

Timing fields are refused on multicam clips because they would slip the clip out of sync; property fields stay editable, and angle changes go through change_cam.

blendMode.description: Video/image clips only. How the clip composites over the tracks below it (Premiere/Photoshop blend modes). 'normal' is the default (source-over) and clears any blend. Rejected on text/audio clips.

clipIds.description: Clip IDs to update. The property values below apply to every clip in this list.

crop.description: Static source crop for video, image, Lottie, and nested timeline clips. Partial; omitted edges keep current values. Insets are 0–1 of the source (left/top/right/bottom). All zeros restore the full source. Clears crop keyframes. Not for split screen/PIP/grid — use apply_layout.

bottom.description: Inset from the source bottom edge, 0–1.

left.description: Inset from the source left edge, 0–1.

right.description: Inset from the source right edge, 0–1.

top.description: Inset from the source top edge, 0–1.

edgeRounding.description: Video, image, Lottie, and nested timeline clips only. Uniform edge rounding from 0 (square) to 1 (half the shorter visible edge).

edgeSoftness.description: Video, image, Lottie, and nested timeline clips only. Edge feathering from 0 (crisp) to 1 (half the shorter visible edge).

fadeInFrames.description: Fade length from the clip's first frame. 0 clears it. Multiplies existing opacity/volume keyframes.

fadeInInterpolation.description: Curve for the fade in. Omit to keep the current curve.

fadeOutFrames.description: Fade length ending at the clip's last frame. 0 clears it. fadeInFrames + fadeOutFrames must not exceed the resulting clip duration.

fadeOutInterpolation.description: Curve for the fade out. Omit to keep the current curve.

opacity.description: Opacity 0.0-1.0. Clears any existing opacity keyframes.

transform.description: Single-clip only — not for split screen, PIP, or grid (use apply_layout). Partial transform; omitted fields keep current values. Static rotation uses clockwise degrees and clears rotation keyframes.

trimEndFrame.description: SOURCE-media offset, NOT a timeline frame: frames trimmed off the end of the source, in PROJECT frames. Do not derive it with a linear speed formula when speedCurve is present.

trimStartFrame.description: SOURCE-media offset, NOT a timeline frame: frames trimmed off the start of the source — measured in PROJECT frames (the timeline's fps, same units as startFrame/durationFrames; never the source's own fps). For uniform-speed clips, source offset = trimStartFrame + (P − startFrame) × speed. Do not use that linear formula when speedCurve is present.

volumeDb.description: Volume in decibels from −60 through +15. 0 dB keeps source level; −60 dB is mute. Clears existing volume keyframes.

tools.name: edit_speed
tools.description:
Change one clip's playback speed as one atomic, undoable edit. Use uniform for a constant rate, curve for exact speed points matched to the footage, or reset for normal 1× playback. This is the only tool for clip speed; do not use set_clip_properties or set_keyframes.

Inspect the source to locate the important visual moments before authoring a curve. Points use 0–1 visible-source position so they remain attached to content when the resulting timeline duration changes. Use rate for a joined point. Use rateBefore and rateAfter only for an intentional abrupt split at that point. curveAfter controls interpolation from this point's outgoing rate to the next point's incoming rate. The first and last positions must be exactly 0 and 1.

The edit preserves visible source content, applies the same curve to aligned linked media, ripples eligible contiguous followers, and refuses the entire operation if any affected clip cannot move safely. Re-read get_timeline to verify the resulting speedCurve and placement.

action.description: Speed edit to perform. Exactly the fields documented for that action are allowed.

clipId.description: Clip ID from get_timeline. Linked media is updated automatically.

points.description: Required for curve. Complete replacement point list in strictly increasing visible-source positions. New gaps must span at least one source frame. Reuse adjacent point IDs to retain or widen shorter gaps created by trimming.

curveAfter.description: Interpolation to the next point; default smooth. Omit on the final point.

id.description: Optional existing point ID from get_timeline. Reuse it to preserve a trimmed segment’s easing shape; omit it to author a new segment with a deterministic ID.

rate.description: Joined rate. Use this or both split-rate fields, not both.
Required for uniform. Constant playback multiplier.

tools.name: copy_clip_settings
tools.description:
Copy one clip's static settings to one or more clips of the same media type in a single undoable action. Use for requests such as "make these shots look like that one," "use this title style," or "give these audio clips the same treatment."

Choose exactly one target mode. targetClipIds applies to an explicit list and refuses any mismatched media type. targetTrack selects every same-type clip on one stable trackId; add range [startFrame, endFrame) to limit it to clips intersecting that part of the timeline. Track mode excludes the source and mismatched clips, returns compact matched/changed/unchanged/incompatible counts instead of clip IDs, and refuses when no compatible clips match.

Video, image, Lottie, and nested-timeline clips copy transform, crop, opacity, edge rounding/softness, blend mode, and the complete effect stack including color. Text clips copy typography/style, text animation, fill mode, position, rotation, flips, opacity, and effects; target text, word timings, and caption membership stay intact, and the box is refit to the target content. Audio clips copy volume and effects, including denoise. Settings absent from the source clear the corresponding target setting.

This does NOT copy placement, duration, trims, speed, fades, top-level keyframes, media, links, caption groups, or multicam membership. Use set_clip_properties and set_keyframes for temporal changes. Linked audio is a separate audio clip: copy it explicitly using the nested audio.id from get_timeline.

sourceClipId.description: Clip whose current static settings are copied.

targetClipIds.description: Explicit destination clips. Every target must have the same mediaType as the source. Use this or targetTrack, not both.

range.description: Optional [startFrame, endFrame) timeline range. Only intersecting clips are considered; omit for the whole track.

tools.name: set_keyframes
tools.description:
Set animated keyframes on one property of one clip. Replaces the existing keyframe track for that property (pass an empty array to clear). Frames are CLIP-RELATIVE offsets (0 = first frame of the clip), so keyframes follow the clip when it moves. Rows are sorted by frame internally and the LAST row for any duplicate frame wins. Values must be finite numbers. Each row is `[frame, ...values, interp?]` where interp ∈ {linear, hold, smooth} (default smooth).

Properties and their value layouts:
  • volumeDb `[frame, decibels]` — −60 through +15 dB; 0 dB keeps source level and −60 dB is mute
  • opacity `[frame, value]` — value 0.0–1.0
  • rotation `[frame, degrees]` — clockwise degrees
  • position `[frame, topLeftX, topLeftY]` — TOP-LEFT corner in 0–1 normalized canvas coords. NOT the center. (Default static transform centers a full-canvas clip, so top-left of the static is (0, 0); a centered half-size clip has top-left (0.25, 0.25).)
  • scale `[frame, width, height]` — clip's normalized width and height in 0–1 canvas coords (1.0 = fills the canvas axis), NOT a scale factor. Text clips use this same track; use matching width/height ratios for uniform text scale.
  • crop `[frame, top, right, bottom, left]` — animated side insets in 0–1 of the source media. Constant crop belongs on set_clip_properties.
  • blur `[frame, radius]` — whole-layer Gaussian blur from 0–100 px; supported by visual clips including video, images, text, and nested timelines.

Motion keyframes (position/scale/rotation) override the static `transform` value when active.

keyframes.description: Replacement keyframe rows. Empty array clears the track. Row shape depends on property — see tool description.

property.description: Which property's keyframe track to set.

tools.name: apply_layout
tools.description:
Arrange multiple clips into a common multi-video layout (split screen, picture-in-picture, grid) in one undoable action — the fast path for composing several videos in one frame. Use this instead of hand-setting transforms and screenshot-checking alignment with inspect_timeline.

You pick a named layout and assign a clip to each of its slots; the tool computes every transform and crop so each clip FILLS its region edge-to-edge WITHOUT stretching — the source is cropped to the slot's shape (cover), like a layout template the videos are dropped into. Pass fit='fit' to letterbox the clip's visible frame inside its slot instead (no further crop, may leave bars) — use only when the full frame must stay visible (e.g. a screen recording).

The crop is centered by default. When that chops off something important (a face cropped at the forehead, a subject off to one side), bias which part survives: 'anchor' is a coarse shortcut ('top' keeps the top, etc.), while anchorX/anchorY (0–1) give continuous control for in-between framing — e.g. anchorY 0.35 moves the crop only slightly toward the top, not all the way. A clip's existing crop is the source: the layout crops within it, never re-cropping from the full frame. To nudge framing after the fact, restore the source first (set_clip_properties crop all zeros), then re-apply with adjusted anchorX/anchorY — a clip already cropped to the slot's shape has nothing left to reveal.

Two modes (don't mix across slots):
• Place new clips: give each slot a 'mediaRef' (media asset from get_media, or a timelineId to nest) plus top-level startFrame (default 0) and endFrame. Creates one stacked video track per slot at that time range; for PIP the inset is placed on top automatically. Video and nested-timeline clips bring their linked audio.
• Re-layout existing clips: give each slot 'clipIds' — one or more existing clips (video, image, or nested timeline / mediaType 'sequence'), all framed into that slot (handy when a track holds several sequential takes). Only transforms/crop change — timing and tracks are untouched (so existing track order decides stacking).

To animate into the layout, pass motion (slide, push, or overlay) and durationFrames. Prefer push: the keep side fills the frame at 0 then compresses into its slots; incoming enters from direction. slide moves only incoming. overlay fades only incoming. PIP push shrinks the inset from full; PIP slide brings it from off-canvas. A single clip in full swipes in from direction. Motion is keyed at the first frame every slot shows content; takes beginning later hold the finished layout. If direction does not pick a unique slot, left or top stays and incoming still travels from that direction.

Every slot of the chosen layout must be filled. Layouts and their slot names:
  • full — main
  • side_by_side — left, right
  • top_bottom — top, bottom
  • pip_bottom_right / pip_bottom_left / pip_top_right / pip_top_left — main, inset
  • grid_2x2 / grid_3x3 / grid_4x4 — equal cells named rNcN, counting from the TOP-LEFT: row 1 is the top row, column 1 is the left column. So r1c1 is top-left, a 3x3's middle is r2c2, and a 3x3's bottom-right is r3c3
  • main_sidebar — main (70%), sidebar (30%)
  • three_up — left, center, right (three vertical columns)
  • three_stack — top, middle, bottom (three horizontal rows)

direction.description: Incoming edge (default right on splits, bottom on stacks). Keep is chosen from slots and this edge only. If the edge is not unique (e.g. top_bottom + right), left or top stays and incoming still travels from here.

durationFrames.description: Required with motion. Keyframe span in project frames. Must be >= 1 and fit inside every clip playing at the motion start.

endFrame.description: Placement mode only (mediaRef slots). The placed clips occupy [startFrame, endFrame). Required when placing new clips.

fit.description: How each clip fills its slot. 'fill' (default) covers the slot and center-crops the source (no stretch). 'fit' letterboxes the whole source inside the slot.

motion.description: Optional entrance. Prefer push. slide: only incoming travels. push: the keep side also compresses from filling the frame; a PIP inset shrinks from full. overlay: only incoming fades. One clip in full swipes the frame. Requires durationFrames.

slots.description: One entry per slot of the chosen layout. Each entry names a 'slot' and gives exactly one of 'mediaRef' (place a new clip) or 'clipIds' (re-layout existing clip(s) into that slot). Don't mix placement (mediaRef) with re-layout (clipIds) across slots.

anchor.description: Coarse shortcut for which part of the source to keep when cover-cropping (default center). For in-between framing use anchorX/anchorY instead — the named values are just shortcuts for them.

anchorX.description: Fine horizontal framing, 0–1: 0 keeps the left edge, 0.5 centers (default), 1 keeps the right. Only affects slots cropped horizontally. Overrides anchor's x.

anchorY.description: Fine vertical framing, 0–1: 0 keeps the top (e.g. a forehead), 0.5 centers (default), 1 keeps the bottom. Nudge by small amounts (e.g. 0.35) to move the crop gradually. Only affects slots cropped vertically. Overrides anchor's y.

clipIds.description: Existing clip(s) to frame into this slot — video, image, or nested timeline (mediaType 'sequence'). Every listed clip gets this slot's transform/crop (pass one id for a single clip, or several when a track holds sequential takes). Use this OR mediaRef. Clips sharing a slot may sit on the same track; clips in DIFFERENT slots still must not overlap on one track.

mediaRef.description: Asset ID from get_media, or a timelineId to nest as a sequence clip. Use this OR clipIds.

slot.description: Slot name for the chosen layout (e.g. 'left', 'inset', or 'r1c1' for the top-left grid cell).

startFrame.description: Placement mode only (mediaRef slots). Project frame where the layout begins. Default 0.

tools.name: sync_clips
tools.description: Align one or more clips to a reference clip by shifting targets on the timeline — use for dual-system sound (camera + external audio) or multicam. Default mode 'auto' aligns by embedded source timecode when both files carry one (exact, confidence 1.0), falling back to audio cross-correlation otherwise (seeded by capture dates when present); force a method with mode. referenceClipId stays put unless a target would land before frame 0, in which case the whole group shifts right together (reported as shiftedFrames). Returns offsetFrames, confidence (0–1), and method (timecode|audio) per target; refuses weak audio matches. Refused on multicam clips — a group's members are already aligned by its sync maps (manage_multicam).

mode.description: auto (default): timecode when available, else audio. audio/timecode force that method.

referenceClipId.description: Clip the others align to. Stays put.

searchWindowSeconds.description: Optional max ± offset to search in seconds. Omit to search the full feasible overlap.

targetClipId.description: Single clip to align. Use targetClipIds for several.

targetClipIds.description: Clips to align with the reference.

tools.name: manage_multicam
tools.description: Create or ungroup a multicam group. create syncs session media into ordinary stamped timeline clips: one program video track, one audio track per mic, and angle switches through change_cam. Use member kind angle for scratch-camera audio, mic for program audio, and both for a camera whose audio should play. Pin offsetSeconds when correlation cannot align a member. ungroup strips stamps and leaves clips in place.

master.description: angleLabel or mediaRef whose audio clock defines the group. Default: first mic/both member.

members.description: Session source files, at least two.

angleLabel.description: Handle used by change_cam. Default: file name.

kind.description: angle = camera scratch audio, mic = audio in the mix, both = camera plus program audio.

offsetSeconds.description: Pin this member's group-clock offset instead of correlating.

searchWindowSeconds.description: Max ± audio sync search window, seconds (default 240).

startFrame.description: Timeline frame to place the group. Default: timeline end.

groupId.description: Group to dissolve; its clips stay put, unstamped.

tools.name: change_cam
tools.description:
Switch a multicam group's camera angle over timeline frame ranges, full-frame or in a multi-angle layout. Batched entries are one undo step. Ranges where an angle was not recording clamp or skip. Returns switched count, optional clamps/skips/overlayClipIds, and program rows over the touched span.

Each entry is EITHER {range, angle} — full-frame switch — or {range, layout, angles} — PiP/split/grid: angles fill the layout's slots in order (first = the full-frame program slot; fewer angles than slots leaves cells empty), extra angles land as synced overlay clips above the program. A later full-frame entry over the same range clears the layout. Overlay clips are ordinary group clips — restyle with set_clip_properties/apply_layout, remove with remove_clips.

clipId.description: Any clip of the group on the active timeline.

entries.description: Switches to apply, in order. Later entries win on overlap.

angle.description: angleLabel to show full-frame. Omit when using layout.

angles.description: angleLabels in slot order for layout; [0] is the program slot.

layout.description: Multi-angle layout. Grid cells are rNcN counting from the top-left (r1c1 is top-left, row 1 is the top row); shaped layouts name slots by role.

groupId.description: The multicam group (from manage_multicam create or get_timeline's multicamGroups). Or pass clipId.

tools.name: get_multicam
tools.description: Read a multicam group: members (angleLabel, kind, offsetSeconds, confidence, which is master), the current program cut as run-length [angle, startFrame, endFrame) rows in timeline frames, and the track indexes the group occupies. Use it to learn angle labels before change_cam, or to review the cut as one program instead of piecing it together from get_timeline's clips. Window long timelines with startFrame/endFrame.

clipId.description: Any clip of the group on the active timeline.

groupId.description: The multicam group id. Or pass clipId.

startFrame.description: Optional window start for program rows.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Reverts the latest action from the editor's shared undo history, whether the user or agent made it. Call only when that latest action should be reversed. For example, verify a cut with get_transcript, then undo if it overshot and retry with corrected ranges. After undoing, ids and frames returned by the reverted action may be invalid; re-read with get_timeline or get_transcript before editing again. Takes no arguments.
